opportunities.title: Small Research Grants
opportunities.eligibility_summary: BES membership required. Open to researchers from all countries globally; projects can be conducted anywhere in the world. Not available to cover salary of the principal researcher, bench fees or departmental vehicle hire. Requires two reference statements, one personal statement and one supporting letter.
opportunities.summary: Provides up to £5,000 for new and innovative ecological research of the highest international standard, supporting work that advances ecological science.

opportunities.title: Synthesis Grants
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Main applicant must have BES membership (not required for all group members). Groups of 8-15 individuals with a diverse mix of career stages, institutions and international participation, not formed entirely of academic institutions. Requires two statements of support from host institutions.
opportunities.summary: Fast-tracks innovative and impactful research by funding the formation of new two-year synthesis groups that bring together diverse interdisciplinary groups of 8-15 people to analyse and synthesise existing data.

opportunities.title: Long-Term Research Grants

amount.raw: £3,500 in year 1 (first five years' funding), an additional £3,500 in the sixth year; averages £500 per year over a decade

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Must have BES membership. Open to all types of ecologists including conservation practitioners, reserve managers and consultants, as well as university academics. Awarded to individuals, not organisations. Requires one reference statement from a supervisor/employer.
opportunities.summary: Provides a small amount of funding each year for 10 years to enable existing short-term projects with at least 1-2 years of data to be continued long-term, supporting ecological restoration, habitat creation, control of alien species and climate change projects anywhere in the world.

opportunities.title: Pedagogical Research and Development Grants
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Must have BES membership. No geographical restrictions; open to anyone involved in teaching ecology at any level (early years to lifelong learning, formal or informal settings), including those in industry. Projects max 12 months. Awarded to individuals, not organisations. Requires two reference statements. Not for work forming part of a degree/masters/PhD/fellowship.
opportunities.summary: Funds research informing teaching and learning practices to improve learners' experience and promote excellence in ecological education, including evidence-based examples of innovative practice, systematic reviews, exploring emerging education research areas and disseminating best practice.

opportunities.title: Connecting Ecologists with Other Disciplines Grants
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Must have BES membership. Open to PhD students, postdoctoral fellows, early career ecologists, established researchers or employees of other organisations. Must have employer/supervisor approval and a willing host organisation. Undergraduates and masters students are not eligible. Awarded to individuals, not organisations. Requires two reference statements.
opportunities.summary: Promotes interdisciplinary skills by funding up to £20k towards placements in different disciplines and sectors, immersing an ecologist in another professional world (discipline, NGO/charity, public sector, business) for a secondment of up to 12 months.

opportunities.title: Outreach and Engagement Grants
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Lead applicant must have BES membership. Open to individuals, teams and organisations across all experience levels. Projects max 12 months, aimed at a non-academic audience. No restrictions on where applicants come from or where work is carried out.
opportunities.summary: Supports BES members to deliver independent outreach, public engagement and science communication activities that engage public audiences with the excitement, importance and relevance of ecological science, or enhance the skills of others to communicate ecology.

opportunities.title: Annual Meeting Grants 2026
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Must be a BES member at any career stage. Must be a citizen of and based in the Global South. Must be travelling from and returning to the Global South country. Must have applied to present at the BES Annual Meeting. Must be at least three years since last awarded a BES Training and Travel Grant. One reference required.
opportunities.summary: Supports researchers based in Global South countries to attend the BES Annual Meeting in the UK, covering costs directly related to attending the meeting such as registration, transport, food and accommodation. Awards selected by lottery. Application window 17 July - 8 September 2026.

opportunities.title: Training and Travel Grants

amount.raw: maximum £500 for in-person events; maximum £250 for virtual conferences/courses

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Must be a BES member and a PhD student or postgraduate researcher registered on a postgraduate research degree programme (postdocs, undergraduates and masters students not eligible). Must work/study at a university or research institution and work in areas within the BES remit. Must give a presentation if attending a meeting. One statement of support required.
opportunities.summary: Helps PhD students and postgraduate researchers meet the costs of specialist field training courses and to present their work at workshops and conferences. Awards are lottery-based. Next round opens 24 August 2026 and closes 8 September 2026.
